title: Care Assistant
description:
FANTASTIC OPPORTUNITY TO JOIN A PROFESSIONAL HOME CARE PROVIDER:

Are you qualified and experienced in health care?

Would you like a rewarding career while having flexibility?

Do you want to make a positive difference in someone s life and get paid for it?
INTERESTED!
READ ON

£ 12.82/HR, 37.50 Hours per week

If you like working with people and are qualified and have experience of working in the world of social care, take this opportunity and CALL US NOW, we are NOW RECRUITING candidates to join our professional team of care workers. We only employ the very best people who share our passion and who truly want to make a positive difference to others, It s a valuable job that can turn into a rewarding long-term career that helps others while making you feel good about yourself.

OneCare is a growing Home Care provider that has built a reputation for quality. We have clients throughout London that require care and support to help them remain living in the comfort of their own homes.
We are now recruiting care workers to join our professional team of care workers. It is essential that you have relevant home care experience, qualifications, and the knowledge to provide the best quality support to our clients. We encourage and support the professional development of our care workers through training and provide a full induction to successful candidates.
We only employ the very best people who share our passion and who truly want to make a positive difference to others, you should be organized with a flexible and empathetic attitude with an overall passion for care.

F/T AND P/T POSITIONS AVAILABLE FOR DOMICILIARY CARE

Personal attributes:
- To be flexible and adaptable in their working hours
- Caring and diplomatic and have an ability to recognize the signs when the client is stressed and needs support.
-To be enthusiastic, outgoing, reliable, excellent timekeeping, patient, and persistent.

Knowledge and Expertise:
- Care experience
- Some experience in caring for clients in their own home
- RQF Level 6
- English Level B2

We are looking for carers, care workers, and health care assistants for:
- Mornings/Daytime/Evenings

We need carers, care workers, and health care assistants to provide the following services:
- Personal Care
- Domestic Care
- Social Care
- Community Inclusion
- Companionship

Candidates must be eligible to work in the UK and will be required to get an enhanced CRB check.
Please submit your CV to our Recruitment Team OR contact our office between 9:00 am and 5.00 pm, Monday to Friday

Thank you
Onecare-UK

title: Support Worker
description:
Elwood Recruitment are looking for Support Workers in Camden!

Do you have experience supporting adults with learning disabilities? Do you live in Camden or the surrounding areas?

Are you looking for control over your own work schedule? Are you looking for weekly pay?

Elwood Recruitment is seeking experienced Support Workers to deliver high-quality care within residential services supporting adults with learning disabilities. These services operate on a 24-hour basis, requiring a professional, reliable, and compassionate workforce.

Essential Experience: Care & Support Work: 6 Months in the UK

The role involves providing day to day support with daily living tasks, activities and making full use of community opportunities. As part of the care and support team you will assist in maintaining a safe and enabling environment that provides positive experiences to those living within the service.

Candidate Requirements
Applicants should meet the following criteria:
- A minimum of six months experience in care and support work within the UK
- Demonstrable experience supporting adults with learning disabilities
- A genuine commitment to enhancing the wellbeing of vulnerable individuals
- A flexible approach to working hours and shift patterns

Role Responsibilities
Successful candidates will contribute to a structured care environment by:
- Supporting individuals with daily living activities, including personal care, meal preparation, and financial tasks
- Facilitating access to community-based activities and services
- Encouraging participation in social and recreational pursuits such as arts, music, and group events
- Promoting independence while ensuring safety and wellbeing
- Maintaining a positive, respectful, and inclusive living environment

Working Patterns
Flexible scheduling is available, allowing candidates to manage their own availability. Shift patterns typically include:
- Early shifts
- Late shifts
- Long day shifts
- Sleep-in duties
- Waking night shifts

Benefits
- Paid Annual Leave
- Pension Contributions
- FREE Training Development
- Monthly Recognition Awards
- Typical Shift Schedules / Patterns

If you are interested in this opportunity, please submit your application here or contact Elwood Recruitment directly for further information.

title: Communication Support Worker
description:
Location: Carshalton

Start Date: ASAP

Job Type: Part-time / Full-time, Temporary

Salary: From £35 per hour (inclusive of holiday pay)

About the Role

We are seeking an experienced Communication Support Worker (CSW) to provide high-quality support to Deaf and hard-of-hearing learners. The ideal candidate will be confident using British Sign Language (BSL), committed to inclusive education, and able to work collaboratively with teaching staff to ensure learners have full access to the curriculum.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide real-time interpretation between spoken English and BSL (or the learner's preferred communication method)
- Work closely with tutors to support inclusive teaching strategies
- Maintain accurate records, logs, and databases
- Assist learners with understanding verbal instructions, written materials, and classroom tasks
- Support a positive and accessible learning experience for all students

Required Skills & Qualifications
- Level 3 BSL qualification (essential)
- Experience supporting Deaf or hard-of-hearing learners
- Ability to adapt and modify learning materials to meet communication needs
- Ability to promote Deaf awareness among staff and peers
- Strong communication and organisational skills

Why Work With Us?
- Exclusive access to roles in leading FE colleges and training providers
- 1-2-1 support from a Specialist SEN Consultant (CV tips & interview prep!)
- Health Cash Plan & REED Discount Club
- Statutory Sick Pay, Maternity/Paternity/Adoption Pay
- Access to REED Learning & Development programmes
- Eye test and spectacle vouchers

If this role sounds of interest, Apply Today!

title: Healthcare Assistant
salary_text: £13.75 - £14.5 per hour (Including holiday pay, flexible hours)
description:
Healthcare Assistant (Agency) - Leeds Flexible Shifts Weekly Pay

Looking for flexible work that fits around your lifestyle?

Search Consultancy is expanding its Bank Support Worker team in the Leeds area and we're looking for experienced Support Workers to join us.

Whether you're looking to top up your income, fit work around family commitments, or choose when and where you work, we offer flexible agency shifts across a range of high-quality healthcare services.

We're recruiting now with a fast-track recruitment process, next-day video interviews, and a free enhanced DBS for successful applicants (limited-time offer).

The Role

You'll support adults in specialist healthcare settings, working with individuals with mental health needs and learning disabilities. Every shift offers the opportunity to make a genuine difference while gaining experience across a variety of services.

Responsibilities
- Supporting individuals with day-to-day living activities

- Assisting with mobility and safe moving & handling
- Supporting with meals, hydration and personal wellbeing

- Flexibility to work a variety of shifts

What You'll Get
- Competitive hourly pay
- Complete flexibility - choose the shifts that suit you
- Ongoing work available throughout the year
- Free specialist training
- Free enhanced DBS (limited-time offer)
- The opportunity to work across a variety of quality healthcare settings and build your experience

Apply Today

If you're an experienced Support Worker looking for flexible agency work with regular shifts available, we'd love to hear from you.

All roles are subject to an enhanced DBS check and two satisfactory employment references.

Search is an equal opportunities recruiter and we welcome applications from all suitably skilled or qualified applicants, regardless of their race, sex, disability, religion/beliefs, sexual orientation or age.

title: Support Worker
description:
Support Worker

Location: Brentford
Hours: Monday - Friday, 8:30am - 4:30pm
Salary: Competitive Daily Rate / Depending on Experience

Start Date: ASAP / September Start Available

Support Worker- Job Overview

We are currently seeking a dedicated and compassionate Support Worker to join a specialist SEN provision in Brentford, supporting children and young people aged 8-16 with Autism (ASD), ADHD, SEMH and additional learning needs.

This is an excellent opportunity for individuals who are passionate about supporting vulnerable young people and helping them achieve positive educational, emotional and social outcomes within a structured, safe and nurturing environment.

Support Worker-Key Responsibilities
- Provide one-to-one and small group support for students with SEN including ASD, ADHD and autism.
- Support students with emotional regulation, communication and social interaction.
- Assist students both inside and outside of the classroom to encourage engagement and participation.
- Implement behaviour support strategies and de-escalation techniques where required.
- Support teachers and SEN staff with classroom activities and differentiated learning.
- Build positive and trusting relationships with students to promote confidence, wellbeing and independence.
- Monitor student progress, behaviour and wellbeing and report concerns appropriately.
- Support safeguarding procedures and follow all school policies and guidelines.
- Work collaboratively with teachers, therapists, pastoral staff and parents/carers.
- Promote a safe, inclusive and supportive learning environment for all students.

Support Worker-Candidate Requirements
- Experience working with children or young people with SEN, ASD, ADHD or SEMH needs.
- Strong behaviour management and communication skills.
- Calm, patient and resilient approach.
- Ability to build positive relationships with students and staff.
- Understanding of safeguarding and child protection procedures.
- Experience within schools, youth work, care or alternative provisions is desirable.
- Enhanced DBS on the Update Service preferred.

What We Offer
- Supportive and welcoming SEN environment.
- Ongoing training and professional development opportunities.
- Long-term opportunities and career progression.
- Opportunity to make a genuine difference to young people's lives.

title: Autism Support Worker
description:
Autism Support Worker - SEN School - Bromley

Are you passionate about supporting children with autism and looking for a role where you can truly make an impact? A dynamic and growing SEN school in Bromley is seeking a dedicated Autism Support Worker to join their team and support pupils in a nurturing, well-equipped environment in September 2026.

Location: Bromley
Pay: £100-110 per day
Contract: Full-time

When: September 2026

Why This School?
- Easily accessible location with excellent transport connections
- Purpose-built facilities tailored for students with special educational needs
- Small class sizes for more focused, meaningful support
- A friendly, inclusive, and collaborative school culture
- Experienced teaching staff in every classroom
- Competitive Inner London pay rates

The Role

This is a full-time, long-term position starting after the summer break, with the potential to continue beyond the academic year.

As an Autism Support Worker, you'll play a key role in supporting pupils with autism and complex needs. You'll work in a structured, supportive classroom setting, helping students develop academically, socially, and emotionally.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Supporting students on a 1:1 basis or in small groups
- Delivering engaging, personalised activities
- Encouraging independence, confidence, and life skills
- Helping to maintain a calm and positive learning environment

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who:
- Has experience with (or a strong understanding of) ASD and complex needs
- Is patient, empathetic, and approachable
- Feels confident working both one-to-one and within a classroom
- Builds strong relationships with students and colleagues
- Is passionate about supporting children with SEN

Experience is helpful but not essential - attitude, commitment, and willingness to learn are just as important.
- Experience as an Autism Support Worker, Teaching Assistant, or similar role (preferred)
- A genuine interest in supporting children with autism and SEN
- A valid DBS on the update service (or willingness to apply)

title: Behaviour Support Assistant
company: Qualiteach Education Group Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Behaviour Support Assistant - Wandsworth - SEMH School - 95- 115 a day (depending on experience) - Full Time - Immediate Start
- Behaviour Support Assistant - Previous experience supporting pupils with behavioural or SEMH needs required
- Behaviour Support Assistant - Experience working in a SEMH school, PRU or alternative provision desirable
- Behaviour Support Assistant - Must be confident with behaviour management and de-escalation strategies
- Behaviour Support Assistant - Required full time ASAP

Have you previously worked as a Behaviour Support Assistant, Behaviour Mentor or Teaching Assistant?
Do you have experience supporting pupils with behavioural or emotional needs?
Are you able to build positive relationships with young people and promote positive behaviour?

If yes, then this Behaviour Support Assistant role is for you

The Role - Behaviour Support Assistant
Seeking a resilient and proactive Behaviour Support Assistant to support pupils aged 11-16 within a specialist SEMH setting in Wandsworth. You will work closely with teaching staff, pastoral teams and the wider support team to provide 1:1 and small-group support for pupils who require additional behavioural and emotional support. The role involves implementing behaviour support strategies, using de-escalation techniques, promoting emotional regulation and helping pupils remain engaged with their learning. You will act as a positive role model and help pupils develop the confidence and resilience needed to re-engage with education.

The School - Behaviour Support Assistant
This specialist secondary provision is located in Tooting within the London Borough of Wandsworth and is within walking distance of a nearby London Underground station. The school supports pupils with social, emotional and mental health needs and provides a structured, supportive environment focused on behaviour, wellbeing and re-engagement with education. Staff work closely with pupils to build positive relationships and help them achieve their academic and personal potential. The school was judged 'Good' at its most recent Ofsted inspection.

Apply here for this Behaviour Support Assistant role or contact Brandon at Qualiteach for more information!
